title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster
quote: We found that CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki type name DNp09; the kit also lists DNp09 as a hemibrain synonym of DNp71 (ambiguous) and driver_lines.csv lists SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS DNp09;DNp71, so DNp09 (the identically named MANC type) is chosen at medium confidence.
stimulation: 627 nm LED, 0.025 mW/mm2, 10 repetitions of 2 s on / 20 s off
type_coverage: bilateral pair (paper: 'a bilateral pair of DNs')
sensory_condition: 30 mm arena, infrared backlight, automated tracking
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (unspecified; paper refers to FlyLight website)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of stimulations; freezing 85% at low pre-stimulus speed, 55% at high speed
n_flies_note: 80 test flies, 72 controls (no retinal); 800 test stimulation events
notes: Mixed outcome: an initial running bout ('The lag in freezing correlated with an initial increase in walking speed, induced by DNp09 activation (Fig. 6d)'; reduced in controls) followed by freezing; jumps at light offset. Leg fields set unclear because freezing convention (no) and increased-locomotion convention (yes) conflict; no leg tracking (centroid speed only). Cited by the 2025 DN split-GAL4 catalogue (Zung et al.) as a use of the 2018 collection.

title: Moonwalker Descending Neurons Mediate Visually Evoked Retreat in Drosophila
quote: Here, we present data from functional imaging, behavioral epistasis, and unilateral activation experiments that support these hypotheses.
mapping_basis: MDN (moonwalker descending neuron) is itself a MANC type name in type_list.csv.
coordination_notes: turning while walking backward attributed to asymmetric left/right MDN activation (hypothesis supported per abstract)
notes: Paywalled (Cell/ScienceDirect returned 403; not in PMC). Abstract states the hypothesis that 'turning while walking backward might reflect asymmetric activation of the left and right MDNs' and that unilateral activation experiments support it. Cited with outcome by Namiki et al. 2018 (eLife 34272) Discussion: 'Activation of bilateral MDNs cause backward locomotion' / 'the unilateral activation cause backward turning toward the contralateral side'. Effector kind (optogenetic) is an assumption not stated in the abstract; preparation unknown (coded other).

title: Female contact activates male-specific interneurons that trigger stereotypic courtship behavior in Drosophila
quote: the initiation of courtship behavior is significantly correlated with the activation of the transmidline P1 interneurons, the descending P2b interneurons, or both
mapping_basis: Kit lists P2b as a literature synonym of both pIP10 and DNxl053 (ambiguous); the abstract gives no anatomy to choose between them, so UNMAPPED per protocol.
sensory_condition: male placed alone without courting target
coordination_notes: 'an entire series of courtship acts' (acts not itemised in abstract)
notes: Paywalled; abstract only. Correlational MARCM mapping: courtship initiation associated with P1, P2b or both, so P2b's own contribution is not isolated. Cited by Namiki et al. 2018 (eLife 34272) Introduction for DN activation eliciting coordinated actions.
